title: Encore: The benefits of being bilingual, with Viorica Marian, PhD

sentences.en: Speaking of psychology is taking a winter break, so we're rerunning some of our favorite episodes from the paSt.
sentences.zh: 说到《Speaking of Psychology》节目，我们要放个寒假了，所以接下来会重播几期我们过去最喜欢的单集。

sentences.en: Last year, I talked to researcher Viorica Marion about why speaking multiple languages is good for the brain and about how language shapes the way we see the world.
sentences.zh: 去年，我采访了研究员维奥里卡·马里恩，探讨了为什么说多种语言对大脑有益，以及语言如何塑造我们看待世界的方式。

sentences.en: We hope you enjoy this episode from the archives.
sentences.zh: 希望大家喜欢这期往期节目。

sentences.en: Speaking of psychology, we'll be back with new episodes in early January.
sentences.zh: 说到《Speaking of Psychology》，我们将在明年一月初带着新节目回归。

sentences.en: Thank you for listening.
sentences.zh: 感谢收听。

sentences.en: Over the past 40 years, the number of people in the United States who speak a language other than English at home has nearly tripled to 68 million.
sentences.zh: 在过去40年里，美国在家中说非英语语言的人数几乎翻了两番，达到了6800万。

sentences.en: That's about one in every five Americans.
sentences.zh: 大约每五个美国人中就有一个。

sentences.en: And in many other parts of the world, bilingualism and multilingualism are even more common.
sentences.zh: 在世界的许多其他地方，双语和多语现象更为普遍。

sentences.en: In fact, more than half the world's population speaks more than one language.
sentences.zh: 事实上，世界上有一半以上的人口说一种以上的语言。

sentences.en: In recent years, scientists have begun to explore what's going on in the brains of people who are bilingual or multilingual.
sentences.zh: 近年来，科学家们开始探索双语或多语人群的大脑中到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: And they found evidence that speaking multiple languages may have cognitive benefits that
sentences.zh: 并且他们找到了证据，证明会说多种语言可能会带来认知上的益处，

sentences.en: include improving people's executive function abilities and slowing down the progression of age-related dementia.
sentences.zh: 其中包括提高人们的执行控制能力以及延缓与年龄相关的痴呆症的发展进程。

sentences.en: Researchers are also learning more about how the bilingual brain processes language and how the languages we speak shape the way we think and perceive the world.
sentences.zh: 研究人员还在进一步了解双语大脑是如何处理语言的，以及我们所说的语言如何塑造我们的思维和对世界的感知。

sentences.en: So why might speaking multiple languages have such far-reaching benefits?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么会说多种语言会带来如此深远的好处呢？

sentences.en: How does the brain process more than one language at a time?
sentences.zh: 大脑是如何同时处理一种以上语言的？

sentences.en: How do the languages we speak affect the way we see the world and the decisions we make?
sentences.zh: 我们所说的语言如何影响我们看待世界的方式以及我们做出的决定？

sentences.en: And what counts as being bilingual?
sentences.zh: 什么才算作是双语者？

sentences.en: Are people who are fluent in computer code or even math or music bilingual?
sentences.zh: 精通计算机代码、甚至数学或音乐的人算不算双语者？

sentences.en: And finally, if you're interested in the benefits of learning a new language, is it ever too late to try?
sentences.zh: 最后，如果你对学习新语言的好处感兴趣，现在开始尝试会太迟吗？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《Speaking of Psychology》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理学科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Viorika Marion, a professor in the Department of Psychology and Communication
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是西北大学心理学与沟通科学及失调系教授

sentences.en: Sciences and Disorders at Northwestern University.
sentences.zh: 维奥里卡·马里恩博士。

sentences.en: She's a psychologist and cognitive scientist whose research focuses on bilingualism and multilingualism.
sentences.zh: 她是一名心理学家和认知科学家，其研究重点是双语和多语现象。

sentences.en: She studies the relationship between language and memory, as well as how people process spoken and written language.
sentences.zh: 她研究语言与记忆之间的关系，以及人们如何处理口头和书面语言。

sentences.en: Dr. Marion is the author of the recent book, The Power of Language, How the Codes We Use to Think, Speak, and Live Transform Our Minds.
sentences.zh: 马里恩博士是近期出版的新书《语言的力量：我们用于思考、说话和生活的代码如何重塑我们的大脑》的作者。

sentences.en: Dr. Marion, thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 马里恩博士，谢谢你今天能来。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我。

sentences.en: It's good to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: You open your book with an epigraph.
sentences.zh: 你的书是以一句题词开头的。

sentences.en: To have another language is to possess another soul.
sentences.zh: “掌握另一种语言，就是拥有一种新的灵魂。”

sentences.en: Why did you choose that quote?
sentences.zh: 你为什么选择这句名言？

sentences.en: What does it mean to you?
sentences.zh: 它对你意味着什么？

sentences.en: I chose that quote because it reflects on what people who speak two or more languages often
sentences.zh: 我之所以选择这句名言，是因为它反映了会说两种或多种语言的人经常有的

sentences.en: experience, that when they use their different languages, they become slightly different versions of themselves.
sentences.zh: 体验，那就是当他们使用不同的语言时，他们会变成稍微不同版本的自己。

sentences.en: With each language bringing to the forefront different cultural experiences, different memories,
sentences.zh: 每种语言都会把不同的文化经历、不同的记忆、

sentences.en: different aspects of their identity, different relationships, and in a way serving as a filter through which
sentences.zh: 不同的身份认同面、不同的人际关系带到前台，在某种程度上充当了一种滤镜，通过它

sentences.en: they see the world and interact with themselves, with others, and with the world at large.
sentences.zh: 他们看待世界，并与自己、他人以及广阔的世界进行互动。

sentences.en: Now, you speak multiple languages, including Romanian, Russian, and English.
sentences.zh: 你精通多种语言，包括罗马尼亚语、俄语和英语。

sentences.en: How did your own early experiences of language lead you to the work that you're doing now?
sentences.zh: 你早期的语言经历是如何引导你走向现在从事的工作的？

sentences.en: Yeah, so I grew up in a family that spoke Romanian at home in one of the former Soviet republics where Russian was the official language outside the home.
sentences.zh: 是的，我在一个在前苏联加盟共和国之一的家庭中长大，家里在室内说罗马尼亚语，而室外的官方语言是俄语。

sentences.en: So I went to a Russian child care and grew up with both Romanian and Russian in parallel.
sentences.zh: 所以我上的是俄语幼儿园，在成长过程中同时接触罗马尼亚语和俄语。

sentences.en: Then later in school, I started to study English, then in college, French.
sentences.zh: 后来在学校里，我开始学英语，上了大学又学了法语。

sentences.en: Then I learned some Spanish, then I married into a Dutch family, and ended up really being exposed to a variety of languages, which, as you mentioned earlier in your introduction,
sentences.zh: 接着我学了一些西班牙语，后来嫁进了一个荷兰家庭，最终接触到了各种各样的语言，正如你刚才在节目开头所提到的，

sentences.en: is very common, not only in Europe, but in many different parts of the world.
sentences.zh: 这不仅在欧洲，而且在世界的许多不同地方都非常普遍。

sentences.en: In countries, pretty much every continent, people often speak two or more languages from early childhood and then acquire additional languages often later in life.
sentences.zh: 在几乎每个大洲的国家里，人们往往从小就说两种或多种语言，然后在晚些时候通常会习得更多的语言。

sentences.en: So it is very common for the human condition to really be a bilingual, multilingual one.
sentences.zh: 因此，双语和多语状态确实是人类生存状况中非常普遍的一种现象。

sentences.en: When you call someone bilingual, does that mean the person grew up speaking two languages,
sentences.zh: 当你称呼某人为双语者时，这是否意味着这个人从小就会说两种语言，

sentences.en: or can you become bilingual later in life by studying another language and becoming fluent?
sentences.zh: 还是说你可以在晚些时候通过学习另一种语言并达到流利程度来成为双语者？

sentences.en: In other words, I'm looking for a definition.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，我在寻找一个定义。

sentences.en: You can become bilingual at any age, so you don't have to grow up with two languages to be bilingual.
sentences.zh: 你可以在任何年龄成为双语者，所以并不一定非要在成长过程中掌握两种语言才能成为双语者。

sentences.en: You can learn a second language in childhood, in adolescence, in adulthood, and even in your older age.
sentences.zh: 你可以在童年、青春期、成年甚至老年时学习第二语言。

sentences.en: A bilingual is a person who can use two languages.
sentences.zh: 双语者是指能够使用两种语言的人。

sentences.en: A multilingual is a person who knows and can use more than two languages.
sentences.zh: 多语者是指懂得并能使用两种以上语言的人。

sentences.en: So the definition of bilingualism is broad, and it depends really who you talk to, but it's
sentences.zh: 因此，双语现象的定义是很广泛的，这确实取决于你跟谁交流，但它

sentences.en: the ability to encode our thoughts, our ideas, concepts in more than one symbolic system, and
sentences.zh: 是一种能够将我们的思想、想法、概念编码到不止一个符号系统中的能力，

sentences.en: then be able to transmit across time and space these thoughts, these ideas, and have someone else decode them.
sentences.zh: 然后能够跨越时空传递这些思想、想法，并让其他人对其进行解码。

sentences.en: So the more symbolic systems you have at your disposal, the more languages you know.
sentences.zh: 因此，你拥有的符号系统越多，你懂的语言就越多。

sentences.en: What about people who can understand a second language, but they can't actually speak it, or they speak a little of it with great difficulty?
sentences.zh: 那么那些能听懂第二语言，但实际上不会说，或者说得很结巴、很吃力的人呢？

sentences.en: I'm thinking of this.
sentences.zh: 我想到了这个。

sentences.en: My mother grew up in an Italian family at a time when you weren't supposed to speak
sentences.zh: 我母亲在一个意大利家庭长大，当时按规定是不准说

sentences.en: Italian except in the home, and they didn't want their kids to speak Italian, but the kids understood what the parents were saying.
sentences.zh: 意大利语的，除非是在家里，而且他们不希望自己的孩子说意大利语，但孩子们能听懂父母在说什么。

sentences.en: Do you get any of the brain benefits of being bilingual if you are in that situation?
sentences.zh: 如果你处于这种情况，能获得双语带来的任何大脑益处吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So if you are referring to what's known as heritage bilingualism, bilinguals who grow up in a
sentences.zh: 所以如果你指的是所谓的传承双语现象——即在

sentences.en: household where there is a heritage language that their parents or grandparents or their previous
sentences.zh: 家庭中长大的双语者，家里有他们的父母、祖父母或之前的

sentences.en: family, generations of their family spoke, that may be different from the dominant language outside the home.
sentences.zh: 家族几代人所说的一种传承语言，这可能不同于室外的优势语言。

sentences.en: And there are many heritage bilinguals in the United States.
sentences.zh: 美国有很多这样的传承双语者。

sentences.en: The extent of their fluency in the two languages varies, but they do indeed show many of the
sentences.zh: 他们在两种语言中的流利程度各不相同，但他们确实展现出了许多

sentences.en: consequences of knowing two languages that children who grew up with two languages or people who are fluent in both languages show as well.
sentences.zh: 懂两种语言的后果，这些后果与从小就会说两种语言或精通这两种语言的人所展现的相似。

sentences.en: So it's really the type of language experience that you have that can make you a bilingual or multilingual.
sentences.zh: 所以，真正能让你成为双语或多语者的是你所拥有的语言经历类型。

sentences.en: And there are different kinds of bilinguals and multilinguals.
sentences.zh: 双语者和多语者也有很多不同的类型。

sentences.en: Let's talk for a minute about some of the benefits that you researchers have found by studying people who are bilingual or multilingual.
sentences.zh: 我们花一分钟来谈谈你们研究人员通过研究双语或多语人群发现的一些好处。

sentences.en: What are the kinds of benefits that they experience in the way that they think, in the way that their brain functions and maybe even is structured?
sentences.zh: 他们在思考方式、大脑功能甚至大脑结构方面，会体验到哪些类型的好处？

sentences.en: Yeah, so one of the most striking and interesting findings in recent years is that people who
sentences.zh: 是的，近年来最引人注目和最有趣的发现之一是，使用

sentences.en: use two or more languages show a delayed onset of Alzheimer's and other types of dementia.
sentences.zh: 两种或多种语言的人表现出阿尔茨海默病和其他类型痴呆症发病时间的延迟。

sentences.en: They are diagnosed on average four to six years later than monowinguals, depending on the study that you are looking at.
sentences.zh: 根据你所查阅的研究，他们平均比单语者晚四到六年被诊断出患病。

sentences.en: It seems that knowing two or more languages offers some of those protective benefits against the
sentences.zh: 看起来懂两种或多种语言对有时伴随健康衰老出现、

sentences.en: cognitive decline that's sometimes seen with healthy aging and that's regularly seen with dementia.
sentences.zh: 且在痴呆症中经常出现的认知衰退提供了一些保护性益处。

sentences.en: And not only at the individual level, but at the population level, there are now studies that
sentences.zh: 不仅在个体层面，在人口层面，现在也有研究

sentences.en: show that countries in which two or more languages are official languages of the country have a lower
sentences.zh: 显示，将两种或多种语言作为国家官方语言的国家，其痴呆症的发病率

sentences.en: incidence of dementia than countries where one language is the official language of the country.
sentences.zh: 要低于只将一种语言作为国家官方语言的国家。

sentences.en: And there is actually a direct correlation between the number of languages spoken in the country in the incidence of Alzheimer's.
sentences.zh: 事实上，一个国家所使用的语言数量与阿尔茨海默病的发病率之间存在直接的相关性。

sentences.en: So it's a really interesting new finding showing that the consequences of being bilingual or multilingual
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常有趣的新发现，表明双语或多语现象带来的结果

sentences.en: are not only at the level of the individual, but also at the level of society.
sentences.zh: 不仅体现在个体层面，也体现在社会层面。

sentences.en: And actually in my book, The Power of Language, I organize the book is structured into two parts.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在我的新书《语言的力量》中，我把全书结构安排成了两部分。

sentences.en: The first one talks about the self and then the second one talks about society and how both are are not changed by knowing two or more languages.
sentences.zh: 第一部分讲自我，第二部分讲社会，以及这两者是如何因懂两种或多种语言而发生改变的。

sentences.en: In the case of dementia, what seems to be happening is that the constant workouts that our brains receive
sentences.zh: 在痴呆症的案例中，似乎发生的情况是，我们的大脑因为不得不应付多种语言而得到的持续锻炼，

sentences.en: by having to juggle multiple languages is like an exercise for the brain and has this positive consequences.
sentences.zh: 就像是大脑的体操一样，并带来了这些积极的后果。

sentences.en: So one way to describe this is imagine that you have been taking the same bridge or the same road home every day for many years throughout your life.
sentences.zh: 所以描述这一点的一个方法是，想象你一生中多年来每天都走同一座桥或同一条路回家。

sentences.en: You go to work, you come home, you take this road, you go to the store, you go to the pharmacy, wherever you're going, you go back and forth, you always take the same road.
sentences.zh: 你去上班，你回家，你走这条路，你去商店，你去药店，无论你去哪里，你来来回回，你总是走同一条路。

sentences.en: And then one day when you're way back, you discover that that road has collapsed.
sentences.zh: 然后有一天，当你回程时，你发现那条路塌方了。

sentences.en: If that's the only road that exists to your house, then you're in trouble.
sentences.zh: 如果那是通往你家的唯一一条路，那你就麻烦了。

sentences.en: You won't be able to reach your destination.
sentences.zh: 你将无法到达目的地。

sentences.en: But if there are multiple roads that have been built over time, if you know of those roads,
sentences.zh: 但如果在岁月中修建了多条道路，如果你知道那些道路，

sentences.en: then you simply reroute your car and you are able to reach your destination with no problem.
sentences.zh: 那么你只需给汽车重新规划路线，就能毫无问题地到达目的地。

sentences.en: In the same way, if there are multiple languages that you've used throughout your life to encode
sentences.zh: 同样，如果你一生中使用多种语言来编码

sentences.en: memories, to encode experiences, to learn, to live your life in, you can compensate functionally
sentences.zh: 记忆、编码经历、学习并在其中生活，你就可以通过使用这些语言来从功能上补偿

sentences.en: through using those languages for the anatomical deterioration that your brain experiences.
sentences.zh: 你大脑所经历的解剖学上的退化。

sentences.en: So it's not that the bilingual or multilingual brain doesn't experience deterioration.
sentences.zh: 所以并不是说双语或多语的大脑不会经历退化。

sentences.en: It does.
sentences.zh: 它会的。

sentences.en: But people who know two or more languages are able to compensate for it functionally and live a healthy life as if they don't have the same degree of impact for longer.
sentences.zh: 但懂得两种或多种语言的人能够在功能上对此进行补偿，并能更长时间地过着健康的生活，就好像他们没有受到同等程度的影响一样。

sentences.en: And, you know, four to six years might not seem like a lot when you are, I don't know, 20, 18.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，当你大约20岁或18岁时，四到六年可能看起来不算什么。

sentences.en: But when you are older, four to six years is really a big difference and can make a difference from being able to play with your grandchildren or never knowing them.
sentences.zh: 但当你年纪大了，四到六年真的是一个很大的差距，它能决定你是能和孙辈玩耍还是根本不认识他们。

sentences.en: And there is nothing else that we know of other than perhaps exercise that has as strong of an effect
sentences.zh: 据我们所知，除了可能还有运动之外，没有任何其他东西对认知衰退、阿尔茨海默症和痴呆症具有

sentences.en: on a protective effect on cognitive decline and Alzheimer's system and dementia as the effect size of bilingualism and multilingualism.
sentences.zh: 如此强烈的保护作用，能达到双语和多语现象的作用量级。

sentences.en: So it's one of the most remarkable recent findings in the field.
sentences.zh: 所以这是该领域近年来最卓越的发现之一。

sentences.en: So exercise is up there.
sentences.zh: 所以运动也名列其中。

sentences.en: But what about some of these other mentally enriching things that we engage in, such as maybe having more years of education or a challenging hobby?
sentences.zh: 但是，那些能丰富我们精神的其他事物呢，比如接受更多年的教育或培养一个具有挑战性的爱好？

sentences.en: You're saying that being multilingual gives you greater cognitive benefits than those things?
sentences.zh: 你是说多语能力带给你的认知益处比这些还要大吗？

sentences.en: Those are all good.
sentences.zh: 这些都很好。

sentences.en: And you're right that a level of education is a plus.
sentences.zh: 你说得对，教育水平是一个加分项。

sentences.en: Nutrition is a plus.
sentences.zh: 营养是一个加分项。

sentences.en: Engaging and enriching activities is a plus.
sentences.zh: 参与丰富身心的活动是一个加分项。

sentences.en: All of those things are very good.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都非常好。

sentences.en: But based on my review of the literature looking at meta-analysis, it seems like that effect sizes are largest for exercise in bilingualism.
sentences.zh: 但根据我对涵盖元分析的文献的回顾，运动和双语现象的作用量级似乎是最大的。

sentences.en: And what's really interesting about bilingualism and multilingualism is that you don't have to take time out of your life to engage in those activities to see benefits.
sentences.zh: 关于双语和多语现象，真正有趣的是，你不需要从生活中专门腾出时间来从事这些活动就能看到好处。

sentences.en: So, for example, we know that engaging in cognitively enriching benefits,
sentences.zh: 例如，我们知道参与丰富认知的好处，

sentences.en: cognitively enriching activities like Sudoku or, you know, word puzzles or method, just any kind of cognitively challenging activity is beneficial for the brain.
sentences.zh: 参与数独、字谜或任何类型的具有认知挑战性的活动等丰富认知的活动对大脑是有益的。

sentences.en: And it's a good thing to do as we age for our cognitive health.
sentences.zh: 随着我们年龄的增长，这对我们的认知健康是一件好事。

sentences.en: But for all of those, you have to actively take time out of your life to do those things, whether it's reading.
sentences.zh: 但对于所有这些活动，你都必须主动从生活中腾出时间来做，无论是阅读。

sentences.en: And of course, reading is wonderful for you, whether it's doing puzzles, that's all great.
sentences.zh: 当然，阅读对你大有裨益，无论是做字谜，这些都很棒。

sentences.en: But with being bilingual and multilingual, you simply go about your life using one language or another.
sentences.zh: 但对于双语和多语者来说，你只需使用一种或另一种语言继续你的生活。

sentences.en: And you are constantly giving your brain a workout because your brain has to facilitate the language you are using and inhibit the language you are not using and sort of control
sentences.zh: 你一直在给大脑进行锻炼，因为你的大脑必须促进你正在使用的语言，并抑制你没有使用的语言，还要对

sentences.en: the languages you are using at any given time.
sentences.zh: 你在任何特定时间正在使用的语言进行某种控制。

sentences.en: For example, you and I right now are speaking in English.
sentences.zh: 例如，你和我现在都在说英语。

sentences.en: Our brains have to control our output.
sentences.zh: 我们的大脑必须控制我们的输出。

sentences.en: It would do us little good if I suddenly would switch to Spanish or French or Romanian or Russian.
sentences.zh: 如果我突然切换到西班牙语、法语、罗马尼亚语或俄语，对我们没什么好处。

sentences.en: So I have to make sure that I control those.
sentences.zh: 所以我必须确保我控制住它们。

sentences.en: I inhibit those and I facilitate just English.
sentences.zh: 我抑制它们，只促进英语的使用。

sentences.en: And you do this all the time, whether you are reading, you know, a road sign, you're listening
sentences.zh: 你一直在这样做，无论你是在阅读路标，还是在听

sentences.en: to a movie, a song, you're speaking with someone, you're constantly juggling your many languages.
sentences.zh: 电影、歌曲，与人交谈，你都在不断地在你掌握的多种语言之间进行切换。

sentences.en: So this constant experience juggling different languages seems to be having an effect on your executive function that later translates to benefits beyond just language.
sentences.zh: 因此，这种在不同语言之间来回切换的持续体验似乎对你的执行功能产生了影响，这种影响随后转化为超越纯语言层面的好处。

sentences.en: And I have to say that this area of research, not the dementia part, but the executive function part is somewhat controversial.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，这一研究领域，不是痴呆症部分，而是执行功能部分，是有一定争议的。

sentences.en: Not all studies find benefits of bilingualism on executive function.
sentences.zh: 并非所有研究都发现双语对执行功能有益。

sentences.en: And sometimes people up in arms about that.
sentences.zh: 有时人们为此争论不休。

sentences.en: I am not up in arms about that and I can tell you why.
sentences.zh: 我没有为此争论不休，我可以告诉你为什么。

sentences.en: The reason I'm not up in arms about that is because bilingual experience varies.
sentences.zh: 我之所以不争论，是因为双语体验是多样化的。

sentences.en: There are different kinds of bilingualism.
sentences.zh: 双语现象有不同的类型。

sentences.en: Executive function is an umbrella term that includes multiple components.
sentences.zh: 执行功能是一个包含多个组成部分的统称。

sentences.en: So I think asking the question in this absolute ways, does bilingualism benefit executive function or not?
sentences.zh: 所以我认为用这种绝对的方式来提问：双语是否对执行功能有益？

sentences.en: This black or white approach is not the right way to look at things.
sentences.zh: 这种非黑即白的态度并不是看待问题的正确方式。

sentences.en: A better question would be to ask what aspect, what kinds of language experience influence what kind of executive function and under what circumstance?
sentences.zh: 一个更好的问题是：什么样的方面、什么样的语言经历在什么情况下会影响什么类型的执行功能？

sentences.en: It's sort of like thinking about exercise.
sentences.zh: 这有点像思考运动。

sentences.en: I think universally everyone knows that exercise is good for you.
sentences.zh: 我想普遍来说大家都知道运动对你有好处。

sentences.en: We agree that exercise is good for your health and for aging.
sentences.zh: 我们一致认为运动对你的健康和抗衰老有益。

sentences.en: But it's not like every single type of exercise you do will benefit every single type of your health under every single kind of amount and duration.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着你做的每一种单一运动都会在任何数量和持续时间下有益于你健康的每一个方面。

sentences.en: And there are just so many other variables.
sentences.zh: 而且其中涉及的变量实在太多了。

sentences.en: Some things benefit some variables.
sentences.zh: 某些事物对某些变量有益。

sentences.en: Others benefit other variables.
sentences.zh: 其他事物则对其他变量有益。

sentences.en: So taking this absolute black and white approach is really not a good way to do science.
sentences.zh: 所以这种绝对非黑即白的态度，其实并不是做科学的好方法。

sentences.en: I know that we all like simplified yes, no answers, but it's a much more nuanced, complicated issue.
sentences.zh: 我知道我们都喜欢简单的“是”或“否”的答案，但这是一个更加微妙、复杂的问题。

sentences.en: I want to talk for a minute about what goes on in the brains of people who know multiple languages.
sentences.zh: 我想花一分钟时间来谈谈，精通多种语言的人，他们的大脑里到底在发生什么。

sentences.en: Are all of the languages you know always active or is your brain shutting off and sectioning things so that you know that we're speaking English right now?
sentences.zh: 你所知道的所有语言是一直都处于活跃状态，还是说你的大脑会自动关闭并把它们分门别类，好让你知道我们现在说的是英语？

sentences.en: You're not going to slip into Romanian by accident.
sentences.zh: 你不会一不小心就溜出罗马尼亚语来。

sentences.en: Yeah, we used to think that people switch between languages.
sentences.zh: 对的，我们以前曾认为人们会在不同语言之间进行切换。

sentences.en: There was this language switch hypothesis where there was the belief that when you use one language,
sentences.zh: 当时有一个语言切换假说，人们认为当你使用一种语言时，

sentences.en: you're using it, then you're done with it, you switch it off, you switch the other one on, you use that other language.
sentences.zh: 你正在使用它，然后用完了，你把它关掉，把另一种语言打开，然后使用那种语言。

sentences.en: And there's also the belief that different languages are represented in different parts of the brain.
sentences.zh: 人们还认为不同的语言代表着大脑的不同区域。

sentences.en: So you have like a place for English, a place for French, a place for Hebrew.
sentences.zh: 所以你会有一个放英语的地方，一个放法语的地方，一个放希伯来语的地方。

sentences.en: A place for Arabic, whatever language you are using.
sentences.zh: 一个放阿拉伯语的地方，无论你在使用什么语言。

sentences.en: We now know that's not the case.
sentences.zh: 但我们现在知道事实并非如此。

sentences.en: We know that language is distributed throughout multiple areas of the brain.
sentences.zh: 我们知道语言是分布在大脑多个区域的。

sentences.en: It's a network.
sentences.zh: 它是一个网络。

sentences.en: And we also know that we don't ever really switch off our languages.
sentences.zh: 而且我们也知道，我们从来没有真正关闭过我们的语言。

sentences.en: They are constantly coactivated and running in parallel.
sentences.zh: 它们一直在被共同激活并同时运行。

sentences.en: So our brain is this very impressive superorganism that processes information in parallel at all times from multiple modalities.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的大脑是一个非常令人惊叹的超级有机体，它始终在通过多种模式并行处理信息。

sentences.en: And we know this through multiple lines of research, including research that uses eye tracking,
sentences.zh: 我们通过多条研究路线证实了这一点，包括使用眼动追踪技术的研究，

sentences.en: that shows that people who speak multiple languages, when they hear a word in one language, they often make eye movements to objects in their visual display,
sentences.zh: 该研究表明，会说多种语言的人在听到某种语言的一个词时，经常会把视线投向他们视觉显示器中的物体，

sentences.en: in their visual scene that sounds similar in another language.
sentences.zh: 投向他们视觉场景中在另一种语言里听起来相似的物体。

sentences.en: So, for example, if you are an English speaker, and I sit you in front of a bunch of objects on the desk, and I tell you to pick up a marker while recording your eye movements,
sentences.zh: 所以，举个例子，如果你是一个英语使用者，我让你坐在一堆桌上的物品前，并在记录你眼球运动的同时让你拿起一个记号笔（marker），

sentences.en: as you pick up the marker, you will often make eye movements to other objects like marbles, for example, that start with the same word onset, like marker and marbles.
sentences.zh: 当你拿起记号笔时，你的目光往往会扫向其他物品，比如大理石弹珠（marbles），因为它们以相同的词首发音开头，比如 marker 和 marbles。

sentences.en: But if you speak Spanish,
sentences.zh: 但如果你说西班牙语，

sentences.en: you'll make eye movements to other objects that start with the same onset in your language, like a butterfly.
sentences.zh: 你会把视线投向你所说语言中以相同词首发音开头的其他物品，比如蝴蝶。

sentences.en: The Spanish word for butterfly is mariposa.
sentences.zh: 西班牙语中的蝴蝶是 mariposa。

sentences.en: If you speak Russian, you may make eye movements, or you do make eye movements to a stamp, because the Russian word for stamp is marca.
sentences.zh: 如果你说俄语，你可能会——或者说确实会——把视线投向邮票，因为俄语中的邮票是 marca。

sentences.en: So, as you hear marker, you make eye movements to a stamp.
sentences.zh: 所以，当你听到 marker 时，你会把目光投向邮票。

sentences.en: So, people who speak different languages make eye movements towards different objects as they hear language.
sentences.zh: 因此，说不同语言的人在听到语言时，会将视线投向不同的物体。

sentences.en: Different objects in their display, in their visual scene, attract their attention.
sentences.zh: 他们显示器中、视觉场景中的不同物体会吸引他们的注意力。

sentences.en: And we are now even finding that they remember what they had seen differently, depending on the languages they speak.
sentences.zh: 我们现在甚至发现，根据他们所说的语言不同，他们对所见事物的记忆方式也会有所不同。

sentences.en: So, if you ask a Russian speaker, they are much more likely to remember that there was a stamp on that desk,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你问一个俄语使用者，当他们在找记号笔时，

sentences.en: when they were looking for a marker than an English monolingual speaker.
sentences.zh: 他们比只说英语的单语者更有可能记得那张桌子上有一枚邮票。

sentences.en: And the Spanish speaker is more likely to remember that, you know, they saw a butterfly flying around when they were looking for a marker, than if you don't speak Spanish.
sentences.zh: 而西班牙语使用者更有可能记得，你知道的，他们在找记号笔时看到了一只蝴蝶在飞，这比不会说西班牙语的人概率更高。

sentences.en: It's really interesting because it shows us that the languages we speak influence what we see, our perception of the world around us, our perception of reality,
sentences.zh: 这真的很有趣，因为它向我们表明，我们所说的语言会影响我们看到的东西、我们对周围世界的感知、我们对现实的感知，

sentences.en: and influences what we remember later when we think about our environment.
sentences.zh: 并影响我们以后思考周围环境时的记忆。

sentences.en: So, I think back to experiences we've had.
sentences.zh: 所以，我会回想起我们曾经有过的经历。

sentences.en: So, language is this very powerful experience that we filter our world through and our lives through.
sentences.zh: 因此，语言是一种非常强大的体验，我们通过它来过滤我们的世界和生活。

sentences.en: Now, if you grow up in a bilingual household, at what point do you realize that there are two different languages being spoken instead of one big language that encompasses both?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果你在一个双语家庭长大，你在什么时候才会意识到有两门不同的语言在被使用，而不是一门包含两者的庞大语言呢？

sentences.en: That's a good question because it taps into what's known as metalinguistic ability.
sentences.zh: 这是个好问题，因为它触及了所谓的元语言能力。

sentences.en: Metalinguistic ability is the ability to reason about language abstractly.
sentences.zh: 元语言能力是对语言进行抽象推理的能力。

sentences.en: And we all as adults develop it eventually.
sentences.zh: 我们作为成年人，最终都会发展出这种能力。

sentences.en: So, adults know that you can call something, but by any word you want, and it doesn't change what this word is, I might have, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，成年人知道你可以用任何你想要的词来称呼某样东西，这不会改变这个词本身的含义，我可能，你知道的，

sentences.en: a pen and I might call it a pen or a ruchka or a stylo, or however I might call it, and it doesn't change it.
sentences.zh: 有一支钢笔，我可能会叫它 pen、ruchka、stylo，或者随便怎么叫，但这并没有改变它。

sentences.en: But bilingual kids develop this ability to reason about objects and their names in this abstract ways earlier than monolingual kids.
sentences.zh: 但双语儿童比单语儿童更早地发展出了这种以抽象方式对物体及其名称进行推理的能力。

sentences.en: At an early age, they understand that the world and the words we used to refer to the world are not one and the same,
sentences.zh: 在很小的时候，他们就明白世界以及我们用来指代世界的词汇并不是一回事，

sentences.en: that you can change the labels and it doesn't change the object.
sentences.zh: 你可以改变标签，但不会改变物体本身。

sentences.en: So, this is really a foundational skill for cognitive development, being able to reason abstractly about our environment and the labels we used to refer to it.
sentences.zh: 所以，这确实是认知发展的一项基础技能，能够对我们的环境以及我们用来指代它的标签进行抽象推理。

sentences.en: In your book, you write about how for people who are bilingual, the experience of speaking in their native versus their non-native language may be quite different.
sentences.zh: 你在书中写道，对于双语者来说，用母语和非母语说话的体验可能会非常不同。

sentences.en: For example, people may make different moral decisions or access different memories when they're talking in their native versus their non-native language.
sentences.zh: 例如，人们在用母语和非母语交谈时，可能会做出不同的道德抉择或调动不同的记忆。

sentences.en: Can you talk about that?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈这个吗？

sentences.en: What are the connections among language, memory, and emotion that are all at play?
sentences.zh: 语言、记忆和情感之间到底有哪些相互交织的联系？

sentences.en: This is a really rich topic because it does make a big difference in our decision-making and the emotions we feel and how we think about our identity
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常丰富的话题，因为根据我们在任何特定时间所说的语言，它确实会对我们的决策、我们感受到的情感、我们如何思考自己的身份

sentences.en: and how we interact with others, depending on which language we're speaking at any given time.
sentences.zh: 以及我们如何与他人互动产生重大影响。

sentences.en: There is some evidence suggesting that the native language tends to be a more emotional language, tends to be tied to emotions more closely,
sentences.zh: 有一些证据表明，母语往往是一种更具情感色彩的语言，与情感的联系更紧密，

sentences.en: whereas the second language often can be a more logical language or lead to people making decisions that are more logical and utilitarian.
sentences.zh: 而第二语言通常可以是一种更具逻辑性的语言，或者引导人们做出更具逻辑性和功利性的决策。

sentences.en: So in one of these areas of research, scientists were asking bilinguals to make moral decisions in either their native language or their second language.
sentences.zh: 因此，在这些研究领域之一，科学家们要求双语者分别用他们的母语或第二语言做出道德抉择。

sentences.en: And I'll give you an example.
sentences.zh: 我给你举个例子。

sentences.en: You may have heard of the very famous trolley dilemma.
sentences.zh: 你可能听说过那个非常著名的电车难题。

sentences.en: And there are different versions of it, but in this particular version of the trolley dilemma, a trolley is coming down the tracks and there are five workers working on the tracks
sentences.zh: 它有不同的版本，但在电车难题的这个特定版本中，一辆电车正顺着轨道驶来，有五名工人在轨道上作业，

sentences.en: and the trolley is about to run over them and kill them.
sentences.zh: 电车即将撞上他们并夺去他们的生命。

sentences.en: And you are standing on the footbridge above those tracks next to a large person with a large backpack.
sentences.zh: 而你正站在轨道上方的人行天桥上，旁边站着一个背着大背包的大块头。

sentences.en: And if you push the person off the footbridge, the person will die, but that will stop the trolley and will save the lives of these five people.
sentences.zh: 如果你把这个人推下人行天桥，这人会死，但这会拦住电车，并拯救这五个人的生命。

sentences.en: So the question is, is it permissible to sacrifice the life of one person to save the lives of five people?
sentences.zh: 所以问题是，为了拯救五个人的生命而牺牲一个人的生命，这样做是可以接受的吗？

sentences.en: How would you answer that?
sentences.zh: 你会怎么回答？

sentences.en: I hate that dilemma.
sentences.zh: 我讨厌那个困境。

sentences.en: I don't know what I would do.
sentences.zh: 我不知道我会怎么做。

sentences.en: I think I would not be able to push somebody off a bridge.
sentences.zh: 我想我无法把某个人推下桥。

sentences.en: I hate the dilemma too.
sentences.zh: 我也讨厌这个困境。

sentences.en: And I know what you mean.
sentences.zh: 我懂你的意思。

sentences.en: And your answer, it really just depends.
sentences.zh: 你的回答，其实视情况而定。

sentences.en: You can change it.
sentences.zh: 你可以改变它。

sentences.en: A lot of people would say, yeah, I can see how it makes more sense to sacrifice one person for five, but I would never push a person off the bridge or kill a person.
sentences.zh: 很多人会说，是的，我能理解为什么为了五个人牺牲一个人更有意义，但我绝不会把人推下桥或者杀死一个人。

sentences.en: And some people would be more likely to do it if all they have to do is push a button versus push a person.
sentences.zh: 如果他们只需要按一个按钮而不是去推一个人，有些人可能更有可能这么做。

sentences.en: And then it depends if it's five people versus 5,000 people.
sentences.zh: 然后这还要取决于救的是五个人还是五千个人。

sentences.en: There are so many versions of this problem.
sentences.zh: 这个问题有太多的版本了。

sentences.en: But interestingly, it seems that if you ask bilinguals to make this decision in their native language versus their second language, you see differences in how they answer.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，如果你让双语者分别用母语和第二语言来做这个决定，你会发现他们的回答存在差异。

sentences.en: They are much more likely to be guided by what's known as deontological values.
sentences.zh: 他们更有可能受制于所谓的道义论价值观。

sentences.en: So what's inherently morally right or wrong in their native language
sentences.zh: 也就是在他们的母语中，本质上什么是道德上正确或错误的，

sentences.en: and say that they are less likely to sacrifice the life, to kill one person, to sacrifice the life of one person for five than when they're speaking their native language
sentences.zh: 并且比起说第二语言时，他们在使用母语时更不可能为了五个人去牺牲一条生命、去杀死一个人。

sentences.en: versus when they're speaking their second language.
sentences.zh: 而在说第二语言时则相反。

sentences.en: When they're speaking their second language, they are more likely to make a utilitarian decision
sentences.zh: 当他们说第二语言时，他们更有可能做出功利主义的决策，

sentences.en: and decide that you go with a decision that has the greater good.
sentences.zh: 并决定选择符合最大利益的方案。

sentences.en: So this is one set of experiments.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一组实验。

sentences.en: But people have looked at the likelihood of cheating, at medical decisions, at all sorts of decisions, and they are finding that bilinguals tend to make different decisions
sentences.zh: 但人们还研究了作弊的可能性、医疗决策以及各种决策，他们发现双语者倾向于在不同的语言中做出不同的决策。

sentences.en: in one language versus another.
sentences.zh: 在一门语言中与在另一门语言中不同。

sentences.en: And it does seem that the first language just tends to be more closely tied to emotions.
sentences.zh: 而且第一语言确实似乎与情感的联系更加紧密。

sentences.en: And I think many individuals who speak two or more languages often experience it themselves, that they feel a different reaction when someone says,
sentences.zh: 我想许多会说两种或多种语言的人自己也经常深有体会，当有人用母语对他们说“我爱你”，或者当他们自己用母语而不是第二语言说出这句话时，他们会产生不同的反应。

sentences.en: I love you to them in their native language, or when they say it themselves in their native language versus their second language.
sentences.zh: 或者当他们自己用母语而不是第二语言说出这句话时。

sentences.en: So that's a tip out there for your listeners who may be in the relationships with bilinguals or multilinguals to learn some of these key phrases, emotional phrases,
sentences.zh: 所以，给你的听众（他们可能与双语或多语者谈恋爱）的一个小建议是，去学习一些关键短语、情感短语，
